## F1 — Wrong-case keys bypass the unknown-key check, and `Kinds` is silently replaced by the defaults

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/config/config.go:40`, `internal/config/config.go:50`
- Situation: `.benchpress.toml` uses a key that differs only in case from a Go
  field name, e.g. `Kinds = ["x"]`, `Dir = "work"`, or `AREAS = ["maps"]`.
- Happens: BurntSushi's decoder matches those keys to the fields
  case-insensitively, so they are not in `meta.Undecoded()` and no unknown-key
  error is returned. For `Kinds` the value is then lost as well:
  `meta.IsDefined("kinds")` is false because the mapping key is `"Kinds"`, so
  `Load` overwrites the configured list with `DefaultKinds`. A reproduced run
  of `Load` on `Kinds = ["x"]` returned `Kinds:[bug change design idea]` with a
  nil error. `Dir` and `AREAS` are likewise accepted under the wrong case.
- Should: only the exact keys `dir`, `kinds` and `areas` are known; any other
  key is an error naming it, per `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 ("An unknown key is an
  error, so a misspelt key is not silently ignored"). Since `Undecoded` does not
  cover this, validate the top-level names in `meta.Keys()` against the allowed
  set instead.
- Test: none exists; add a case-variant key (at least `Kinds = ["x"]`) that must
  fail `Load`.

## F2 — `FindRoot` treats a directory named `.benchpress.toml` as the config file

- Class: gap
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `internal/config/config.go:63`
- Situation: a directory named `.benchpress.toml` sits at or below the real
  config file, for example `root/.benchpress.toml` (a file) and
  `root/mid/.benchpress.toml/` (a directory), with `FindRoot` called from
  `root/mid/a`.
- Happens: `os.Stat` succeeds for the directory, so `FindRoot` returns `mid` as
  the root; the real config at `root` is shadowed and never found. With no file
  above, `Load` then fails with `read .../.benchpress.toml: is a directory`
  rather than returning `ErrNoRoot`. Both cases reproduced.
- Should: only a directory that holds a regular file named `.benchpress.toml`
  counts as the root; a directory with that name is not the file, so the walk
  should continue upward, per the unit goal and `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 ("the first
  directory holding `.benchpress.toml`").
- Test: none exists; add a test with a `.benchpress.toml` directory below a
  real config file.

## F1 — Appending a field to a CRLF file whose closing `---` has no newline inserts an LF line

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/topic/topic.go:179`, `internal/topic/topic.go:181`
- Situation: a CRLF topic whose closing `---` is the last line and has no
  trailing newline, e.g. `"---\r\nkind: bug\r\narea: maps\r\nstate: open\r\n---"`,

  The same happens with an empty CRLF front matter ending `---` without a
  newline. `TestSetAppendCRLF` does not catch it because its closing `---`
  already ends in `\r\n`.
- Should: keep the file's CRLF style for the appended line, as the work order's
  "CRLF input left CRLF" requires and the handover claims ("`Set` appends with
  the closing `---`'s terminator, so CRLF files stay CRLF"). When the closing
  line has no terminator, use the preceding line's terminator (and only fall
  back to `\n` when the file has no line ending at all).
- Test: none exists; add a `Set` append case whose closing `---` has no final
  newline and that expects `\r\n` before the closing line.

## F1 — Adding an item to a no-item file whose last line has no newline welds the item onto that line

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/next/next.go:123`, `internal/next/next.go:126`
- Situation: `NEXT.md` exists but has no items and no final newline, for example
  `"# Next\n\nSome prose."`, and an item is added with
  `Add(Item{Target: "a.md", Text: "[a](a.md)"})` (or `AddAt(..., 1)`).
- Happens: `Render` appends the stored head lines verbatim and then writes the
  item block without checking that the last head line ended in a newline. The
  result is `"# Next\n\nSome prose.1. [a](a.md)"`: the item is concatenated onto
  the prose instead of forming a line of its own. The same happens with CRLF
  (`"# Next\r\n\r\nSome prose."`), where the separator should be `\r\n`.
- Should: insert a line ending before the block when the last head line has
  none, so the block goes after the last line as `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 says
  ("With no items yet, the block goes after the last line") and the work order's
  no-items case requires. Preserving the file's missing final newline for the
  new last item is fine; the separator before the item is not.
- Test: none exists. `TestAddAppendsAfterLastLine` uses `"Some prose.\n"` and
  `TestNoItems` never adds anything, so neither reaches the failing path. Add a
  test that parses `"# Next\n\nSome prose."`, adds one item, and expects a
  newline before `1. `.

## F2 — A file with mixed line endings does not round-trip byte for byte

- Class: gap
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `internal/next/next.go:49`, `internal/next/next.go:234`,
  `internal/next/next.go:126`
- Situation: an unchanged `NEXT.md` whose first newline is CRLF and whose later
  item line is LF (or vice versa), for example
  `"1. [a](a.md)\r\n2. [b](b.md)\n"`.
- Happens: `newline` takes the style of the first newline only, and `Render`
  writes every item line with that one style. The unchanged file renders as
  `"1. [a](a.md)\r\n2. [b](b.md)\r\n"`: the second line's terminator changed.
  The handover acknowledges that mixed files will not round-trip, but the work
  order's *Done when* requires "a round trip of an unchanged file byte for byte"
  without limiting it to uniform files.
- Should: an unchanged file should render identically, including a file with
  mixed terminators. Preserve each item's original terminator when rendering a
  parsed item (or state the limitation in the order/design rather than claiming
  the round-trip requirement is met).
- Test: none exists. `TestRoundTrip`, `TestRoundTripCRLF` and
  `TestRoundTripNoFinalNewline` all use a single terminator style. Add a mixed
  LF/CRLF round-trip case.

## F1 — A plan whose file name is not plain ASCII is never found on a branch

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/repo/repo.go:109`, `internal/repo/repo.go:116`
- Situation: a branch-only plan with a UTF-8 name, e.g. `docs/plans/café.md`
  committed on `other` and not present in the working tree, then
  `Find(ctx, "docs/plans/café.md")`.
- Happens: `git ls-tree -r --name-only` C-quotes unusual bytes by default
  (`core.quotePath=true`), so its output line is
  `"docs/plans/caf\303\251.md"`, quotes and escapes included. `branchHolds`
  keys `held` by that raw line, so `held["docs/plans/café.md"]` is false and
  `Find` returns a nil location. I reproduced it against a temporary
  repository with the package itself: `locations = []string(nil)`. Lint then
  reports `plan-gone` (an error, exit 1) for a plan that is on a local branch.
- Should: compare against the path as git spells it: run `ls-tree -z` and split
  on NUL (`-z` is still `ls-tree`, so the command restriction holds), or pass
  `-c core.quotePath=false`; then the branch holding the plan is reported.
  `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 says the plan is found when the path exists "in the tree
  of any local branch", and the work order's *Done when* requires the
  second-branch-only case to be found.
- Test: none exists; every test uses ASCII names. Add a branch-only
  `docs/plans/café.md` and expect `[]string{"other"}`.

## F2 — Any `for-each-ref` failure inside a repository is silently reported as "not a repository"

- Class: design
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `internal/repo/repo.go:73` (the blanket `return found, nil`),
  `internal/repo/repo.go:98`
- Situation: a real repository where `git for-each-ref` fails for a reason
  other than "not a git repository" — for example a corrupt `.git/packed-refs`,
  or git's "detected dubious ownership" refusal when a checkout is owned by
  another user (CI, containers).
- Happens: `branches` returns the error, `Find` discards it with
  `return found, nil`, and only the working-tree hits are returned. A planned
  topic whose plan lives only on a branch is then reported `plan-gone`, and the

  repository whose `packed-refs` has a bad line: `locations = []string(nil),
  err = <nil>`, where git prints `fatal: unexpected line in .git/packed-refs`.
- Should: the work order only promises "outside a git repository ... without an
  error"; inside one, a git failure should surface as an error so `lint`/`ls`
  can report it. Distinguishing the two needs a decision the order did not make
  (identify the not-a-repository error from stderr, or allow a command other
  than the two the *Done when* names), so this is not just a one-line fix. The
  handover lists the limitation; it still produces a false `plan-gone`.
- Test: none exists. Add a case that makes `for-each-ref` fail in a real
  repository (for example the bad `packed-refs` line above) and expect `Find`
